mainTopic: The four signs of a kosher locust, and רב אחאי's source for including a locust with a long head.
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא on ויקרא 11:22, which names kosher locusts and adds 'למינהו' (after its kinds) to each. The ברייתא follows a pattern: 'I only know a species with feature X. How do I know one with feature Y?' Using סלעם, it shows that a locust with a smooth forehead can be kosher. Using חרגול, it shows that one with a tail can be kosher too. For a locust with a long head, it builds a בנין אב from ארבה, חרגול and סלעם: any creature with four legs, four wings, jumping legs, and wings covering most of its body is kosher. It then adds that the creature must also be called חגב, which excludes the צרצור. It also must have all the signs. רב אחאי attacks the בנין אב, because all three source species have short heads, and he shows that this kind of difference does block the comparison. Instead, he proves that the word סלעם is extra and applies it, through אם אינו ענין, to teach that the long-headed locust is kosher.

steps.title: The vineyard bird is included with the ארבה
steps.stepSummary: The ending of the previous line: the למינהו after ארבה includes the ציפורת כרמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The word 'after its kinds' that follows ארבה comes to include] the vineyard bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its first point: the word למינהו next to ארבה brings in a species called the ציפורת כרמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציפורת כרמים is like the ארבה because its forehead is not smooth. So far, then, we only know about kosher locusts whose forehead is not smooth. That limit sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird. Here it is the name of a kind of locust.
Vineyards
The 'vineyard bird', a kosher locust species similar to the ארבה

phrases.english: the vineyard bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ארבה derivation that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציפורת כרמים is a kosher locust, included through the למינהו after ארבה.

steps.title: What about a locust with a smooth forehead?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that a species with a smooth forehead is also kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about a species that comes without a smooth forehead. From where do I know that a species that comes with a smooth forehead is kosher too?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that what we have learned so far covers only locusts without a smooth forehead. It asks for a source for locusts that do have one, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארבה and the ציפורת כרמים both lack a smooth forehead. So we might think a smooth forehead is a sign that a locust is not kosher. The question asks where we learn that this is not so.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have [a source for]. This opens a 'how do we know more?' question.
The one that comes, meaning a species that shows up with these features
A bald, smooth forehead
From where [do we know]?

phrases.english: I have only one that comes
and does not have a smooth forehead.
From where do we know one that comes and has a smooth forehead?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הַבָּא וְאֵין לוֹ גַּבַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the limit of what step 1 taught and asks for more.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a locust with a smooth forehead can be kosher.

steps.title: The סלעם teaches about smooth foreheads
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק names סלעם (the ניפול), which has a smooth forehead, and its למינהו includes the אושכף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'סלעם'; this is the ניפול. 'After its kinds' comes to include the אושכף.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the next name in the פסוק, סלעם, which is a locust with a smooth forehead. The word למינהו adds the אושכף, which is similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the תורה names a kosher locust that has a smooth forehead, a smooth forehead does not make a locust forbidden. The extra word למינהו widens the list to other species like the סלעם.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
One of the four kosher locusts named in the פסוק
The common name for the סלעם
After its kinds. It widens the law to similar species.
A locust species with a smooth forehead, like the סלעם

phrases.english: The verse says: "solam"
this is the nippul,
"after its kinds" comes to include the ushkaf.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סלעם (ניפול) has a smooth forehead and is kosher. Its למינהו includes the אושכף.

steps.title: What about a locust with a tail?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists what is covered so far and asks how we know that a species with a tail is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about species with or without a smooth forehead, and species without a tail. From where do I know that a species with a tail is kosher?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats everything learned so far and notices that none of those locusts has a tail. It asks for a source for one that has a tail, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forehead question is now settled both ways. A new feature comes up: every species named so far lacks a tail. So we need a source that a locust with a tail can be kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A tail
It has
It does not have

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא הַבָּא וְאֵין לוֹ גַּבַּחַת,
phrases.english: And I have only one that comes and has no smooth forehead,
or one that comes and has a smooth forehead.
One that comes and has no tail,
from where do we know one that comes and has a tail?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא הַבָּא וְאֵין לוֹ גַּבַּחַת הַבָּא וְיֵשׁ לוֹ גַּבַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on steps 1 and 3 and asks about a new feature.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a locust with a tail can be kosher.

steps.title: The חרגול teaches about tails
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק names חרגול (the רשון), which has a tail, and its למינהו includes the כרספת and the שחלנית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'חרגול'; this is the רשון. 'After its kinds' comes to include the כרספת and the שחלנית.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the third name in the פסוק, חרגול, which is a locust with a tail. Its למינהו adds two more species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a kosher locust named by the תורה has a tail, having a tail does not make a locust forbidden. Here למינהו includes two species, the כרספת and the שחלנית.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the four kosher locusts named in the פסוק
The common name for the חרגול, a locust with a tail
A locust species with a tail
Another locust species with a tail

phrases.english: The verse says: "chargol"; this is the rashon,
"after its kinds" comes to include the karsefet
and the shachlanit.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חרגול (רשון) has a tail and is kosher. Its למינהו includes the כרספת and the שחלנית.

steps.title: What about a locust with a long head?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists everything covered so far and asks how we know that a species with a long head is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know about species with or without a smooth forehead, with or without a tail, and without a long head. From where do I know that a species with a long head is kosher?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the full list again and points out that no species so far has a long head. It asks for a source, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forehead and tail are both settled now. The new feature is head length, since every locust mentioned so far has a short head. The next step answers this with a בנין אב built from the three species already named, not from another name in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Head
Long
Its head is long

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא keeps the same pattern each time. It lists what is covered so far, notices a new feature, and uses the next named locust plus למינהו to show that the feature does not make a locust forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא הַבָּא וְאֵין לוֹ גַּבַּחַת,
phrases.english: And I have only one that comes and has no smooth forehead,
one that comes and has a smooth forehead;

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא וְאֵין לוֹ זָנָב, הַבָּא וְיֵשׁ לוֹ זָנָב.
phrases.english: one that comes and has no tail, one that comes and has a tail.
One that comes and its head is not long,
from where do we know one that comes and its head is long?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא הַבָּא וְאֵין לוֹ גַּבַּחַת הַבָּא וְיֵשׁ לוֹ גַּבַּחַת הַבָּא וְאֵין לוֹ זָנָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on steps 3 and 5 and asks about a further feature.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a locust with a long head can be kosher.

steps.title: A general rule built from three species
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the long-head question with a בנין אב drawn from ארבה, חרגול and סלעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: build a general rule from all three. The ארבה is not like the חרגול, and the חרגול is not like the ארבה. Neither of them is like the סלעם, and the סלעם is not like either of them. What they all share is four legs, four wings, jumping legs, and wings that cover most of the body. So any species with these four signs is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 6, about a long-headed species. It builds a general rule (בנין אב) from the three species named in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three species looks different from the others, so none of their special features can be what makes them kosher. Only the features all three share can count. Those are four legs, four wings, jumping legs, and wings covering most of the body. Any species with those four signs is included, even if its head is long.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule built from one or more cases written in the Torah
Literally 'appearance'; the special feature of a case
The feature that all the cases have in common
Jumping legs

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the four signs of a kosher locust that the rest of the סוגיא will test.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתָּ: הֲרֵי אַתָּה דָן בִּנְיַן אָב מִשְּׁלׇשְׁתָּן,
phrases.english: You will say: You derive a general rule from the three of them,
phrases.notes: The three are the ארבה, חרגול and סלעם, all named in the פסוק.

phrases.english: the feature of the ארבה is not like the feature of the חרגול,
and the feature of the חרגול is not like the feature of the ארבה,
and the feature of neither of them is like the feature of the סלעם,
and the feature of the סלעם is not like either of theirs.
What they all have in common

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע רַגְלַיִם, וְאַרְבַּע כְּנָפַיִם,
phrases.english: is that each has four legs and four wings,
and jumping legs, and its wings cover most of its body;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע רַגְלַיִם, וְאַרְבַּע כְּנָפַיִם,
phrases.english: so too, anything that has four legs and four wings,
and jumping legs, and its wings cover most of its body, is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ: הֲרֵי אַתָּה דָן בִּנְיַן אָב מִשְּׁלׇשְׁתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the long-head question raised in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בנין אב from ארבה, חרגול and סלעם. Any species with their four shared signs is kosher, including a long-headed one.

steps.title: The צרצור seems to have all four signs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that the צרצור also has the four signs, so the rule would seem to permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this צרצור has four legs, four wings, jumping legs, and wings covering most of its body. Should it be permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own new rule. The צרצור fits all four signs, so the rule would make it kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בנין אב said any creature with the four signs is kosher. The צרצור meets all four, yet the ברייתא assumes it should not be permitted. So the rule on its own seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of insect that looks like a locust
'One might think'; introduces a possible but wrong conclusion
Permitted

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא הַצַּרְצוּר הַזֶּה יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע רַגְלַיִם, וְאַרְבַּע כְּנָפַיִם,
phrases.english: But doesn't this צרצור have four legs and four wings,
and jumping legs, and its wings cover most of its body?
One might think it should be permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the בנין אב from step 7 against a creature it should not include
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The צרצור has all four signs, so the rule would wrongly permit it

steps.title: The word חגב requires the name חגב
steps.stepSummary: The word חגב in the פסוק adds a condition: the creature must be called חגב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'חגב', which teaches that its name must be חגב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא solves the צרצור problem with the word חגב in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having the four signs is not enough. The creature must also be known by the name חגב. The צרצור is not called that, so it stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of locust named in the פסוק; here, the name the creature must have

phrases.english: The verse states: 'חגב', meaning that its name must be חגב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the צרצור problem from step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a further requirement from a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any creature with the four signs, like the צרצור, is permitted
steps.terutzMaskana: The creature must also be called חגב

steps.title: Maybe the name alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether a creature called חגב is kosher even without the signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the key is the name חגב, maybe a creature called חגב is kosher even without all these signs?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the opposite worry. Now that the name matters, maybe the name is all that matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step added the name as a condition. That could suggest the name alone decides, with no signs needed. This step brings up that wrong reading so it can be ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs; physical features that show whether a creature is kosher

phrases.english: But if its name must be חגב,

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֵין בּוֹ כׇּל הַסִּימָנִין הַלָּלוּ?
phrases.english: one might think it is kosher even if it does not have all these signs?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שְׁמוֹ חָגָב, יָכוֹל אֵין בּוֹ כׇּל הַסִּימָנִין הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on step 9 by asking whether the name is now the only test
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the name decides, maybe the signs are no longer needed

steps.title: Both the name and all the signs are needed
steps.stepSummary: The word למינהו teaches that all the signs are still required.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'למינהו', which teaches that it is not kosher unless it has all these signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with the word למינהו. Even a creature called חגב needs all the signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two conditions now work together. The creature must be called חגב and must also have all four signs. This closes the ברייתא's chain of derivations.

keyTerms.meaning: 'After its kind'; a word in the פסוק used here to require all the signs
'Unless it has'; it is not kosher until the condition is met

steps.whatToRemember: A kosher locust needs both: the four signs (four legs, four wings, jumping legs, wings covering most of the body) and the name חגב.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'after its kind'

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כׇּל הַסִּימָנִין הַלָּלוּ.
phrases.english: meaning it is not kosher unless it has all these signs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 and completes the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Joins the two requirements: the name and the signs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The name חגב alone is enough
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the name חגב and all the signs are needed

steps.title: רב אחאי: the three species also have short heads
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי attacks the בנין אב: the three species share another feature, a short head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי challenges this: what about these three? They also have heads that are not long. So how can you learn from them that a long-headed species is kosher?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי now challenges the ברייתא's בנין אב from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בנין אב only works if the cases share nothing that could be the real reason for the law. ארבה, חרגול and סלעם all have short heads. So maybe a short head is also needed, and the proof for a long-headed species fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges; raises an objection that knocks down a proof
'What about these?'; points to a feature that makes the source cases special
'Since they'; introduces that special feature
A long head

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחאי is not denying the four signs. He is saying the three species might share a fifth feature, a short head, that the בנין אב ignored.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥai challenges this:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהָנָךְ, שֶׁכֵּן אֵין רֹאשָׁן אָרוֹךְ?
phrases.english: What about these, which are special in that their heads are not long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the בנין אב from step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The בנין אב that includes long-headed species
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All three source species have short heads, so a short head may also be required

steps.title: A possible defense: four shared signs are enough
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי suggests a defense: once the four signs match, we include the species and don't look for other differences.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: since they match in four signs, we include them and do not raise objections.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי raises a possible answer to his own challenge. He brings it up only so he can reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that matching on all four signs is enough to include a species. A difference like head length would then not block the comparison. This would save the בנין אב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would say'; introduces a possible answer that will then be rejected
We bring in; we include
We raise an objection

phrases.english: And if you would say:
since they match in four signs,
we include them and do not raise objections

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁווּ בְּאַרְבַּע סִימָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the challenge in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested defense: matching all four signs outweighs other differences
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A short head might be a required feature
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: the four signs alone decide, so head length doesn't matter

steps.title: Then the Torah would not need to write חרגול
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי rejects the defense: if four signs were enough, חרגול could have been learned from ארבה and סלעם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the חרגול also matches them. The Torah should not have written it, and we could have learned it from the ארבה and the סלעם!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי knocks down the defense from step 13. He shows it would make one of the words in the פסוק unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If four shared signs were enough to include a species, the חרגול could have been learned from ארבה and סלעם, since it has the same four signs. Yet the Torah wrote חרגול anyway. That suggests we do look for other differences, so the challenge from step 12 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so'; shows where a suggestion would lead
'It should not be written'; the Torah would not need to write it
'And let it come from'; it could be learned from another source

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, חַרְגּוֹל נָמֵי דְּשָׁווּ לְהוּ,
phrases.english: If so, the חרגול also matches them,
so let the Torah not write it, and let it be learned from the ארבה and the סלעם!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, חַרְגּוֹל נָמֵי דְּשָׁווּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense offered in step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that four shared signs are enough to include a species
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the word חרגול in the פסוק unnecessary

steps.title: The defense fails, so the short-head objection stands
steps.stepSummary: The Torah wrote חרגול because it has a tail and could not be learned from ארבה and סלעם. So any real difference matters, and the long-headed grasshopper cannot be learned from species with short heads.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you have to say it could be refuted: what about these, that they have no tail? So too here it can be refuted: what about these, that their heads are not long?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי explains why the Torah really needed to write חרגול: it has a tail, so it cannot be learned from tailless species. That brings back his objection about the long head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If extra differences did not matter, חרגול would not need its own word in the פסוק. Since it does have its own word, a difference like having a tail must be enough to block learning one species from others. A long head is that kind of difference too, so the בנין אב from ארבה, סלעם and חרגול falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted; there is a way to knock down the comparison

phrases.english: Rather, it can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן אֵין לָהֶן זָנָב.
phrases.english: What about these, which have no tail?
phrases.notes: "These" are ארבה and סלעם. חרגול has a tail, so it's different from them.

phrases.english: So too it can be refuted:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן אֵין רֹאשָׁן אָרוֹךְ?
phrases.english: What about these, whose heads are not long?
phrases.notes: Now "these" are all three species: ארבה, סלעם and חרגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן אֵין לָהֶן זָנָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes step 14. It explains why חרגול had to be written, and that brings back the objection from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole בנין אב that was used to include the long-headed grasshopper.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A real difference blocks the comparison, like a tail for חרגול. The long head is that kind of difference.

steps.title: רב אחאי: the word סלעם is extra
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי gives a new source. The Torah did not need to write סלעם, because it could have been learned from ארבה and חרגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחאי said: סלעם is extra. Let the Torah not write סלעם, and let it be learned from ארבה and חרגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי gives up on the בנין אב. He claims the word סלעם is extra in the פסוק, and he sets up how it could have been learned from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a word in the Torah is not needed for its own case, it must be teaching something else. Here, סלעם could have been learned from what ארבה and חרגול have in common. The next step shows why that learning would work.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra; not needed for its plain meaning
"The Merciful One"; the Torah or ה׳ who wrote it

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Achai said:
Solam is extra.
Let the Merciful One not write "solam,"
and let it be learned from arbeh and chargol.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחַאי: סׇלְעָם יַתִּירָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The בנין אב failed in step 15, so רב אחאי offers a different source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The long-headed grasshopper is learned through a בנין אב from the three listed species.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is learned from the extra word סלעם.

steps.title: Neither objection against learning סלעם works
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי shows that any objection to one source species is answered by the other. So סלעם really could have been learned from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what objection could you raise? "What about ארבה, which has no smooth forehead?" Here is חרגול, which has one. "What about חרגול, which has a tail?" Here is ארבה, which has no tail.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי proves that סלעם could be learned from ארבה and חרגול. Every objection against one of them is answered by the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source species has one feature that סלעם does not share. But each of those features is missing in the other source species. So no single feature explains why both are kosher, and only the four shared signs remain. Since סלעם has those signs, it could have been learned without being written.

keyTerms.meaning: You refute; you raise an objection
The common feature; learning from what two sources share

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 15. There the objection worked because the new species was different from all the sources. Here each objection is answered, because the other source species does not have that feature either.

phrases.english: For what objection could you raise?
"What about arbeh, which has no smooth forehead?"
Here is chargol, which has a smooth forehead.
"What about chargol, which has a tail?"
Here is arbeh, which has no tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim from step 16 that סלעם could have been learned from the other two.
steps.raayaObject: That the word סלעם is extra.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The common-feature reasoning from ארבה and חרגול: each objection is answered by the other species.

steps.title: The extra סלעם teaches that the long-headed grasshopper is kosher
steps.stepSummary: Since סלעם was not needed for itself, the Torah wrote it to teach that the grasshopper with a long head is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the סלעם that the Torah wrote? If it is not needed for its own case, apply it to the one with the long head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי finishes his source. The extra word סלעם is used to teach about the long-headed grasshopper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule אם אינו ענין: a word the Torah did not need for its own case is moved to teach a different case. This avoids the problem of the long head, because nothing is being compared anymore. The כשרות comes straight from a word in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own matter; a rule for reading an extra word
For itself; for its own case
Apply it to a different matter

steps.whatToRemember: The בנין אב could not include the long-headed grasshopper, because a long head is a real difference. רב אחאי's final source is the extra word סלעם, which could have been learned from ארבה and חרגול. Through אם אינו ענין it teaches that the long-headed one is kosher.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that when a comparison breaks down, the גמרא can still find the הלכה in an extra word in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Why do I need the solam that the Merciful One wrote?
If it is not needed for its own matter,
apply it to the one whose head is long.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from steps 16 and 17: since סלעם is extra, it teaches something new.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The long-headed grasshopper is kosher, and the source is the extra word סלעם read through אם אינו ענין.
